entries.note: Neither the expectations nor the standard for meeting them is specified sufficiently for a shared test.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and independent evaluations establishing that an LLM alone achieves general human-level cognitive competence would falsify the claim.
entries.note: “On their own” restricts the technology covered; it does not supply a separate triggering event.

entries.test: Publicly documented scaling experiments and independent capability evaluations would test whether scaling existing LLM methods alone suffices to achieve AGI.
entries.note: This asserts a causal limitation of scaling; finite failures would not conclusively establish that limitation.

entries.test: Comparisons of prominent AI figures’ earlier public predictions with their statements around June 2024 would show whether they reduced their commitments or expectations.
entries.note: The appended Kurzweil clarification undermines one example, but Marcus still asserts the broader retreat.

entries.test: Dated internal-model evaluations subsequently made public, technical disclosures, or on-record accounts would establish whether OpenAI had a GPT-5 substantially ahead of its public models in June 2024.
entries.note: The surrounding quotation gives “mind-blowing” a plain comparative reading: substantially ahead of publicly available models. Marcus endorses this inference himself.

entries.test: Public statements after the post through the end of 2025, compared with the same figures’ earlier AI predictions, would show whether further downward revisions occurred across that period.
entries.note: “Expect” expresses a firm forecast, and its deadline has passed.
